performance.note: Diagnostic precriterion only: at least3% lower all40 callback sum plus final readback drain than the faster original arm; both callback40 and drain-inclusive41 p95/max may not regress against either original arm. Quality, literal equivalence, positive baked usage and cleanup must also pass. Injected tests are never accepted. No default adoption or FPS claim.

report.note: 8851 genuine-memory QA only. Fresh owned Renderer/Art/native player and initial max-three-model NPC preparation per original/manual/original arm. Original on-demand species loads remain enabled; actual runtime model/pending maxima are reported. Main ready records are borrowed by identity and never loaded, masked or released through a mutating path. Forty fixed .12-second catch-up callbacks include their first draw; batch-eight rAF yields are reported separately. This is a renderer combat harness without app HUD, audio or persistence, not presented FPS. Certification and lifecycle wrappers are inside render timing in every arm; no Canvas-stage, native-stage or frame-cost observer is installed. Literal per-frame checkpoint/effects/motion/commands/events and both RNG states are compared outside timers. Final whole-canvas readback and PNG export follow the measured loop. Existing twelve-state/two-selected-cell pixel QA is separate evidence, not proof for every source frame. Shared URL decode caches and the live product caches remain resident; fresh instances do not imply cold driver/URL caches. Owned native pending promises are followed through late success/failure for retirement. A failed player Promise.all can have unobservable sibling requests; that failure is explicitly cleanup-unproven rather than called complete. Timings are CPU call wall, not GPU duration or peak memory. No product optimization is adopted by this utility.

readbackStorage.note: Three sequential final-canvas readback arrays and at most three PNG strings are retained until comparison, then raw arrays are dropped; source-pixel storage only, not a peak-memory measurement.
